'''''The Grand Budapest Hotel''''' is a 2014 [[comedy-drama]] film<!--CONSULT THE TALK PAGE before changing the genre. Your change WILL be reverted if you change it without discussion.--> written and directed by [[Wes Anderson]]. The film's seventeen-actor [[ensemble cast]] is led by [[Ralph Fiennes]] as Monsieur Gustave H., famed [[concierge]] of a twentieth-century mountainside resort in the fictional country of Zubrowka. After being framed for the murder of a wealthy [[dowager]] ([[Tilda Swinton]]), he and his recently befriended protégé Zero ([[Tony Revolori]]) embark on a quest for fortune and a priceless [[Renaissance art|Renaissance]] painting amidst the backdrop of an encroaching [[Fascism in Europe|fascist regime]]. Anderson's American Empirical Pictures produced the film in association with [[Studio Babelsberg]], [[Searchlight Pictures|Fox Searchlight Pictures]], and [[Indian Paintbrush (company)|Indian Paintbrush]]'s [[Scott Rudin]] and [[Steven Rales]]. Fox Searchlight supervised the commercial distribution, and ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'}}s funding came from Indian Paintbrush and German government-funded tax rebates.

Anderson and longtime collaborator [[Hugo Guinness]] conceived ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' as a fragmented tale following a character inspired by a mutual friend. They initially struggled in brainstorming, but the experience touring Europe and researching the literature of Austrian novelist [[Stefan Zweig]] shaped their vision for the film. ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' draws visually from Europe-set mid-century [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]] films and the United States [[Library of Congress]]'s [[photochrom]] print collection of alpine resorts. Filming took place in [[eastern Germany]] from January to March 2013. [[The Grand Budapest Hotel (soundtrack)|The film's soundtrack]] was composed by French composer [[Alexandre Desplat]], incorporating symphonic and [[Russian folk music|Russian folk]]-inspired elements and expanding on his earlier work with Anderson. The film explores themes of [[fascism]], nostalgia, friendship, and loyalty. Further discourse analyzes the function of color as a storytelling device.

''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' premiered in competition at the [[64th Berlin International Film Festival]] on February 6, 2014. It was released in theaters in March to widespread critical acclaim, and grossed $174.6 million worldwide at the box office, becoming Anderson's highest-grossing film. It was nominated for nine awards at the [[87th Academy Awards]] including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], winning four, and received [[List of accolades received by The Grand Budapest Hotel|numerous other accolades]]. Since its release, ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' has been assessed as one of the [[List of films voted the best|greatest films]] of the twenty-first century. In 2025, the film was selected for preservation in the United States [[National Film Registry]] by the [[Library of Congress]] as being "culturally, historically or aesthetically significant", and is currently the most recently-released film to be selected.

==Plot==
<!-- KEEP PLOT SUMMARY WITHIN 700 WORDS PER [[WP:FILMPLOT]] -->
In a cemetery in the former nation of Zubrowka,{{efn|Zubrowka is depicted as an [[alpine country]] located somewhere between [[Central Europe|Central]] and [[Eastern Europe]]. According to newspapers shown in the film, Zubrowka was a [[constitutional monarchy]] (the Empire of Zubrowka) at least until late 1932, when a neighboring fascist state annexed it during a period of war. In 1936, the country was liberated, and by 1950, it had become a [[socialist republic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://imgur.com/gallery/ZDyFi/comment/1474868899|title=Newspapers & documents from "The Grand Budapest Hotel"|website=imgur.com|access-date=10 November 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lilianalambriev.com/work/the-grand-budapest-hotel|title=Chapter 5. The Grand Budapest Hotel, Graphic Design for the Film|website=www.lilianalambriev.com|date=November 13, 2014 |access-date=10 November 2020|archive-date=November 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116152834/https://www.lilianalambriev.com/work/the-grand-budapest-hotel|url-status=live}}</ref> The opening titles introduce the region in 2014 as "The former Republic of Zubrowka, Once the seat of an Empire."}}<!--Please before deleting this note consider discussing it on the talk page.--> a young woman visits the shrine of a renowned writer, known simply as "Author", carrying a copy of his bestselling novel ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''. The book, written in 1985, recounts the author's 1968 visit to the once lavish, then drab Grand Budapest Hotel during a bout of [[writer's block]]. There he meets its proprietor, Zero Moustafa, who divulges his [[rags to riches]] story over dinner.

In 1932, Zero flees his war-ravaged country to work as a [[Bellhop|lobby boy]] for Monsieur Gustave H., the philandering [[concierge]] at the Grand Budapest Hotel. Gustave seduces the hotel's old, wealthy residents, including [[dowager]] Madame D., with whom he has had a nearly two-decade affair. Shortly after her last visit, Gustave learns from Zero that Madame D. has mysteriously died. He and Zero visit Schloss Lutz, her estate, to pay their respects; they encounter her surviving relatives at the reading of her will by her attorney, Deputy Vilmos Kovacs. Kovacs announces that she has bequeathed a famous [[Renaissance painting]], ''[[Boy with Apple]]'', to Gustave. Madame's son, Dmitri, is outraged and demands Gustave's arrest. Gustave and Zero abscond with the painting.

Madame D.'s butler, Serge, makes a deposition implicating Gustave in her death. He goes into hiding and Gustave is arrested on suspicion of murder. Gustave befriends a gang during his imprisonment, and the men plot their escape. He has Zero place digging tools inside pastries made by Mendl's apprentice baker, Zero's girlfriend, Agatha. Gustave and the others dig their way out and disperse. Dmitri deploys his hitman, J. G. Jopling, to kill Kovacs and Serge's sister, who conceals her brother's whereabouts.

When Zero and Gustave are reunited, they set out to prove Gustave's innocence with the assistance of a fraternity of concierges known as the Society of the Crossed Keys. They locate Serge, and a meeting is orchestrated for the three. Zero and Gustave learn Serge was pressured to frame Gustave by Dmitri to cover up evidence incriminating Dmitri as the true perpetrator of Madame D.'s murder. Serge tells them that Madame D. had a missing second will which would only become effective if she was murdered. Jopling arrives and kills Serge, leaving Gustave and Zero without a witness. After a chase, Gustave dangles off a cliff at Jopling's mercy. Zero rescues Gustave by pushing Jopling off the cliff, and the two men flee, closely trailed by Zubrowkan police.

Gustave, Zero, and Agatha arrive at the Grand Budapest to find it converted into a military headquarters. Agatha sneaks in to retrieve ''Boy with Apple''; as she is leaving, Dmitri enters the hotel and spots her with the painting. Gustave and Zero rush to save Agatha from Dmitri. He opens fire on them, initiating a melee with Zubrowkan troops. Agatha's attempt to escape leaves her and Zero hanging from a balcony before falling, safely, into a van full of pastries.

Madame's second will, which makes Gustave the beneficiary of her fortune, is found attached to the back of ''Boy with Apple''. Gustave is exonerated in court, after which Dmitri disappears. Zero takes over as concierge and marries Agatha in a ceremony officiated by Gustave. While traveling by train, the three encounter thuggish soldiers who try to arrest Zero, but Gustave attempts to fend them off and they shoot him dead. Zero inherits Gustave's fortune and retains the hotel in memory of Agatha, who died from Prussian [[grippe]] with their infant son.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meenan |first=David |date=October 29, 2022 |title=The Grand Budapest Hotel Ending Explained: An Enchanting Old Ruin |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1067683/the-grand-budapest-hotel-ending-explained-an-enchanting-old-ruin/ |access-date=October 7, 2023 |website=[[/Film]]}}</ref>

Anderson's sightseeing in Europe was another source of inspiration for ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} visual motifs.<ref name="Seitz102">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=102}}</ref> The writer-director visited Vienna, [[Munich]], and other major cities before the project's conception, but most location scouting began after the [[2012 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes]] premiere of his coming-of-age drama ''[[Moonrise Kingdom]]'' (2012). He and the producers toured [[Budapest]], small Italian [[spa town]]s, and the Czech resort [[Karlovy Vary]] before a final stop in Germany,<ref name=Seitz102 /> consulting hotel staff to develop an accurate idea of a real-life concierge's work.<ref name=db />

Anderson desired an English actor to play Gustave, and Fiennes was an actor he sought to work with for several years.<ref name=db /> Fiennes, surprised by the offer, was eager to depart from his famously villainous roles and found Gustave's panache compelling.<ref name="Ny2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/02/movies/wes-anderson-evokes-nostalgia-in-the-grand-budapest-hotel.html |title=Casting Shadows on a Fanciful World |last=Itzkoff |first=Dave |date=February 28, https://web.archive.org/web/20200503151724/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/02/movies/wes-anderson-evokes-nostalgia-in-the-grand-budapest-hotel.html |archive-date=May 3, 2020 |access-date=October 25, 2019}}</ref> Fiennes said he was initially unsure how to approach his character because the extent of Anderson's oversight meant actors could not improvise on set, inhibiting his usually spontaneous performing style.<ref name="Seitz67">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=67}}</ref> The direction of Gustave's persona then became another question of tone, whether the portrayal be [[Camp (style)|camp]] or understated.<ref name=Ny2 /><ref name="Seitz72">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=72}}</ref> Fiennes drew on several sources to shape his character's persona,<ref name="Dog">{{Cite web |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/grand-budapest-hotel-interview-with-ralph-fiennes-and-tony-revolori/ |title=Grand Budapest Hotel Interview with Ralph Fiennes and Tony Revolori |last=Crow |first=David |date=March 5, 2014 |website=[[Den of Geek]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20191026034238/https://www.denofgeek.com/us/movies/the-grand-budapest-hotel/233527/grand-budapest-hotel-interview-with-ralph-fiennes-and-tony-revolori |archive-date=October 26, 2019 |access-date=October 25, 2019}}</ref> among them his triple role as [[History of the Jews in Hungary|Hungarian-Jewish]] men escaping fascist persecution in the [[István Szabó]]-directed drama ''[[Sunshine (1999 film)|Sunshine]]'' (1999), his brief stint as a young [[bellhop|porter]] at [[Brown's Hotel]] in [[London]],<ref name=latgbh /> and the experience reading ''The World of Yesterday''.<ref name="latgbh">{{Cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-et-mn-en-ralph-fiennes-20141125-story.html |title=The Envelope: Ralph Fiennes on nostalgia, heart in Wes Anderson's 'Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Dawes |first=Amy |date=November 25, 2014 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20191026021239/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-et-mn-en-ralph-fiennes-20141125-story.html |archive-date=October 26, 2019 |access-date=October 25, 2019}}</ref> [[Johnny Depp]] was reported as an early candidate in the press, claims which Anderson denied,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/09/29/johnny-depp-grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson_n_1925444.html?guccounter=1 |title=Johnny Depp & 'The Grand Budapest Hotel'? Wes Anderson Says Actor Is Not In The Movie |last=Ryan |first=Mike |date=September 29, 2012 |website=[[HuffPost]] |access-date=September 6, 2018 |archive-date=September 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200912160544/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/johnny-depp-grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson_n_1925444?guccounter=1 |url-status=live }}</ref> despite later reports that scheduling conflicts had halted negotiations.<ref name="conflict">{{Cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/ralph-fiennes-talks-wes-andersons-377685 |title=Ralph Fiennes in Talks for Wes Anderson's 'Grand Budapest Hotel' |last=Kit |first=Borys |date=October 9, 2012 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191031204543/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/ralph-fiennes-talks-wes-andersons-377685 |archive-date=October 31, 2019 |access-date=October 31, 2019}}</ref>

Casting director Douglas Aibel was responsible for hiring a suitable actor to play young Zero. Aibel's months-long search for prospective actors proved troublesome as he was unable to fulfill the specifications for an unknown teenage actor of [[Arabs|Arab]] descent.<ref name="afi">{{cite web|title=American Film|website=American Film |url=https://americanfilm.afi.com/issue/2014/3/cover-story|access-date=September 24, 2025}}</ref> "We were just trying to leave no stone unturned in the process."<ref name=vf1 /> Filmmakers held auditions in Egypt, Lebanon, Israel, France, England, and the United States before revising the role's ethnicity.<ref name="Seitz42">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=42}}</ref><ref name=vf1 /> Eventually the filmmakers narrowed their search to Tony Revolori and his older brother Mario, novices of Guatemalan descent, and Tony landed the part after one taped audition.<ref name="vf1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2015/02/grand-budapest-hotel-casting |title=How The Grand Budapest Hotel Cast Its Most Anderson rehearsed together for over four months before the start of filming to build a rapport.<ref name="atlantic">{{Cite web |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2014/03/tony-revolori-grand-budapest-hotel-perfecting-his-mustache/358847/ |title=Tony Revolori of 'The Grand Budapest Hotel' on Perfecting His Murray Abraham (2014) |date=February 25, 2014 |last=[[F. Murray Abraham|Abraham, F. Murray]] |type=Press interview |publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |time=1:57–2:00}}</ref>

[[Saoirse Ronan]] joined ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' in November 2012.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sneider |first=Jeff |url=https://variety.com/2012/film/news/saoirse-ronan-to-star-in-budapest-hotel-1118061592/ |title=Saoirse Ronan to star in 'Budapest Hotel' |date=November 2, 2012 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=October 26, 2019 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191031015925/https://variety.com/2012/film/news/saoirse-ronan-to-star-in-budapest-hotel-1118061592/ |archive-date=October 31, 2019}}</ref> Though a longtime Anderson fan, Ronan feared the [[deadpan]], theatrical acting style characteristic of Anderson's films would be too difficult to master.<ref name="upi">{{Cite web |url=https://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/Movies/2015/01/25/Saoirse-Ronan-Grand-Budapest-director-Wes-Anderson-was-very-secure-in-his-vision/4781422213149/ |title=Saoirse Ronan: 'Grand Budapest' director Wes Anderson was 'very secure in his vision' |last=Butler |first=Karen |date=January 25, 2015 |website=[[United Press International]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20191030030720/https://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/Movies/2015/01/25/Saoirse-Ronan-Grand-Budapest-director-Wes-Anderson-was-very-secure-in-his-vision/4781422213149/ |archive-date=October 30, 2019 |access-date=October 29, 2019}}</ref> She was reassured by the director's conviction, "He guides everyone extremely well. He is very secure in his vision and he is very comfortable with everything he does. He knows it is going to work."<ref name=upi /> The decision to have Ronan play Agatha in her native [[Irish accent]] was Anderson's idea, after experimenting with German, English, and American accents; they felt an Irish accent projected a warm, feisty spirit into Agatha.<ref name="Dog2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/interview-with-saoirse-ronan-and-adrien-brody-on-the-grand-budapest-hotel/ |title=Interview with Saoirse Ronan and Adrien Brody On The Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Crow |first=David |date=March 6, 2014 |website=Den of Geek |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20191029151320/https://www.denofgeek.com/us/movies/the-grand-budapest-hotel/233558/interview-with-saoirse-ronan-and-adrien-brody-on-the-grand-budapest-hotel |archive-date=October 29, 2019 |access-date=October 29, 2019}}</ref>

===Filming===
[[File:Kaufhaus Görlitz (20350152403).jpg|thumb|alt=Atrium of a large, multilevel building of a defunct department store flagship. Note the damaged ceiling in the background| Atrium of the defunct [[Görlitz Department Store|Görlitzer Warenhaus]] (pictured in 2015), which doubled for the Grand Budapest Hotel lobby]]

The project was director of photography [[Robert Yeoman]]'s eighth film with Anderson. Yeoman participated in an early scouting session with Anderson, recording footage with stand-in film crew to assess how certain scenes would unfold.<ref name="asc">{{Cite web |url=https://theasc.com/ac_magazine/March2014/TheGrandBudapestHotel/page1.html |title=5-Star Service |last=Stasukevich |first=Iain |date=March 2014 |website=[[American Society of Cinematographers]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190920224036/https://theasc.com/ac_magazine/March2014/TheGrandBudapestHotel/page1.html |archive-date=September 20, 2019 |access-date=September 20, 2019}}</ref> Yeoman drew on [[Vittorio Storaro]]'s dramatic lighting techniques in the romantic musical ''[[One from the Heart]]'' (1982).<ref name=ind2 /><ref name="filmmag2">{{Cite web |url=https://filmmakermagazine.com/93700-i-dont-want-to-sound-negative-about-digital-dp-robert-yeoman-on-nab-the-grand-budapest-hotel-and-shooting-film/#.XYVK64wpCfA |title="I Don't Want to Sound Negative About Digital": DP Robert Yeoman on NAB Show, The Grand Budapest Hotel and Shooting Film |last=Mulcahey |first=Matt |date=April 8, 2015 |website=Filmmaker |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190920220247/https://filmmakermagazine.com/93700-i-dont-want-to-sound-negative-about-digital-dp-robert-yeoman-on-nab-the-grand-budapest-hotel-and-shooting-film/%23.XYVMeNLLfK5 |archive-date=September 20, 2019 |access-date=September 20, 2019}}</ref> Filmmakers shot ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' in ten weeks,<ref name=db /> from January to March 2013 in [[eastern Germany]],<ref name=thrcredits /><ref name="guard">{{Cite news |last=Seymour |first=Tom |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/mar/04/grand-budapest-hotel-tony-revolori |title=The Grand Budapest Hotel: the kid stays in the picture |date=March 4, 2014 |work=The Guardian |access-date=October 31, 2019 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20191031173340/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/mar/04/grand-budapest-hotel-tony-revolori |archive-date=October 31, 2019 }}</ref> where it qualified for a tax rebate financed by the [[German government]]'s Federal Film Fund and [[Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg]].<ref name="thrcredits">{{Cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson-412241 |title=Wes Anderson Starts Shoot for 'The Grand Budapest Hotel' in Berlin |last=Roxborough |first=Scott |date=January 14, 2013 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131022234706/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson-412241 |archive-date=October 22, 2013 |access-date=September 17, 2019}}</ref><ref name="thewrap">{{Cite web |url=https://www.thewrap.com/grand-budapest-hotel-cracking-german-financing-crafting-dazzling-vfx/ |title='Grand Budapest Hotel' Cracks German Financing, While Crafting Dazzling VFX |last=Lang |first=Brent |date=April 8, 2014 |website=[[TheWrap]] |access-date=September 17, 2019 |archive-date=October 19, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191019015045/https://www.thewrap.com/grand-budapest-hotel-cracking-german-financing-crafting-dazzling-vfx/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url= https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/germany-cuts-funding-again-film-716750 |title= Germany Cuts Funding (Again) for Film Tax Incentive |last=Roxborough |first=Scott |date=July 4, 2014 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200503031514/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/germany-cuts-funding-again-film-716750 |archive-date=May 3, 2020 |access-date=May 2, 2020}}</ref> They also found Germany attractive because the production base was geographically confined, facilitating efficient logistics,<ref name="Seitz105">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=105}}</ref> but the frigid weather and reduced daylight of early winter disrupted the shooting schedule, compounded by the slow [[film stock]] used for the camerawork. To rectify the issue, the producers used artificial lighting, expedited the daytime work schedule, and [[day for night|filmed night scenes at dusk]].<ref name="ind2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2015/01/wes-andersons-dp-robert-yeoman-on-bringing-the-grand-budapest-hotel-to-life-66637/ |title=Wes Anderson's DP Robert Yeoman |last=Bernstein |first=Paula |date=January 4, 2015 |website=Indiewire |access-date=September 6, 2018 |archive-date=August 27, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180827075547/https://www.indiewire.com/2015/01/wes-andersons-dp-robert-yeoman-on-bringing-the-grand-budapest-hotel-to-life-66637/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Principal photography]] took place at the [[Babelsberg Studio]] in suburban [[Berlin]] and in [[Görlitz]], a mid-sized border town on the [[Lusatian Neisse]] on Germany's eastern frontier.<ref name="NatGeo">{{Cite web |url=https://blog.nationalgeographic.org/2014/03/27/spoiler-alert-you-cant-really-stay-at-the-real-grand-budapest-hotel-but-we-can-tell-you-everything-about-it/ |title=Spoiler Alert: You Can't Really Stay at the Real Grand Budapest Hotel (But We Can Tell You Everything About It) |last=McPherson |first=Angie |date=March 27, 2014 |website=[[National Geographic]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190920153051/https://blog.nationalgeographic.org/2014/03/27/spoiler-alert-you-cant-really-stay-at-the-real-grand-budapest-hotel-but-we-can-tell-you-everything-about-it/ |archive-date=September 20, 2019 |access-date=April 1, 2014}}</ref> The filmmakers staged their largest interior sets at the vacant twentieth-century [[Görlitz Department Store|Görlitzer Warenhaus]], whose [[Atrium (architecture)|atrium]] doubled for the Grand Budapest Hotel lobby. The top two floors housed production offices and storage space for cameras and wardrobe.<ref name=NatGeo /><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/make-wes-anderson-movie-trusted-cinematographer-robert-yeoman/ |title=How to make a Wes Anderson movie, by his trusted cinematographer Robert Yeoman |last=White |first=Adam |date=January 9, 2018 |website=The Telegraph |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190920215410/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/films/0/make-wes-anderson-movie-trusted-cinematographer-robert-yeoman/ |archive-date=September 20, 2019 |access-date=September 20, 2019}}</ref> Anderson at one point considered buying the Warenhaus to save it from demolition.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/berlin-how-wes-anderson-discovered-677336 |title=Berlin: How Wes Anderson Discovered His Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Roxborough |first=Scott |date=February 5, 2014 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190920234716/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/berlin-how-wes-anderson-discovered-677336 |archive-date=September 20, 2019 |access-date=September 20, 2019}}</ref> He and the producers eyed vacant buildings because they could exercise full artistic control, and scouting active hotels that often enforce heavy shooting restrictions would call into question ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} integrity.<ref name=ind2 /> Exterior shots of the eighteenth-century estate Hainewalde Manor and interior shots of [[:de:Schloss Waldenburg (Sachsen)|Schloss Waldenburg]] stood in for the Schloss Lutz estate.<ref name="Seitz143">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=143}}</ref> Elsewhere in Saxony, production moved to [[Zwickau]]—shooting at the [[Osterstein Castle (Zwickau)|Osterstein Castle]]—and the state capital [[Dresden]], where scenes were filmed at the [[Zwinger (Dresden)|Zwinger]] and the Pfunds Molkerei creamery.<ref name=NatGeo />

===Cinematography===

Yeoman shot ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' on [[35 mm movie film|35&nbsp;mm film]] using [[List of motion picture film stocks#Vision3 color negative (ECN-2 process 2007–present)|Kodak Vision3 200T 5213]] film stock from a single [[Arricam|Arricam Studio]] camera provided by [[Arri]]'s Berlin office.<ref name=asc /> His approach entailed the use of a Chapman-Leonard Hybrid III [[camera dolly]] for [[tracking shot]]s and a [[geared head]] to achieve most of the film's rapid [[whip pan]]s. For whip pans greater than 90 degrees, the filmmakers installed a fluid head from [[Mitchell Camera|Mitchell Camera Corporation]]'s OConnor Ultimate product line for greater fidelity.<ref name=asc /> Anderson requested Yeoman and project [[key grip]] Sanjay Sami focus on new methods for shooting the scenes.<ref name=asc /> Thus they used the Mad About Technology Towercam Twin Peek,<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 8, 2019 |title=GMA debuts P63-million state-of-the-art news set, technology for election coverage |url=https://businessmirror.com.ph/2019/05/08/gma-debuts-p63-million-state-of-the-art-news-set-technology-for-election-coverage/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190509041017/https://businessmirror.com.ph/2019/05/08/gma-debuts-p63-million-state-of-the-art-news-set-technology-for-election-coverage/ |archive-date=May 9, 2019 |access-date=February 23, 2022 |website=[[BusinessMirror]]}}</ref> a telescoping camera platform, to traverse between floors, sometimes in lieu of a [[crane shot|camera crane]]. For example, when a lantern drops to the basement from a hole in the cell floor in the Checkpoint Nineteen jailbreak scene, the filmmakers suspended the towercam upside-down, a setup which allowed the camera to descend to the ground.<ref name=asc />

''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' uses three [[aspect ratio (image)|aspect ratios]] as framing devices which streamline the film's story, evoking the aesthetic of the corresponding periods.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Laskin |first=Nicholas |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2015/09/watch-video-essay-explores-the-impact-of-different-aspect-ratios-in-film-260072/ |title=Watch: Video Essay Explores The Impact Of Different Aspect Ratios In Film |date=September 9, 2015 |work=IndieWire |access-date=November 15, 2019 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191115133510/https://www.indiewire.com/2015/09/watch-video-essay-explores-the-impact-of-different-aspect-ratios-in-film-260072/ |archive-date=November 15, 2019}}</ref><ref name="Seitz213">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=213}}</ref> The multifarious structure of ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' emerged from Anderson's desire to shoot in 1.37:1 format, also known as [[Academy ratio]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://slate.com/culture/2014/03/grand-budapest-hotel-aspect-ratios-new-wes-anderson-movie-has-three-different-widths-here-s-why.html |title=The Aspect Ratios of The Grand Budapest Hotel |last1=Haglund |first1=David |last2=Harris |first2=Aisha |date=March 6, 2014 |website=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191117002951/https://slate.com/culture/2014/03/grand-budapest-hotel-aspect-ratios-new-wes-anderson-movie-has-three-different-widths-here-s-why.html |archive-date=November 17, 2019 |access-date=November 16, 2019}}</ref> Production used Academy ratio for scenes set in 1932, which, according to Yeoman, provided the filmmakers with greater-than-routine headroom. He and the producers referred to the work of [[Ernst Lubitsch]] and other directors of the period to acclimate to the compositions produced from said format.<ref name=asc /> Filmmakers formatted modern scenes in standard 1.85:1 ratio, and the 1968 scenes were captured in widescreen 2.40:1 ratio with Technovision [[Cooke Optics|Cooke]] [[anamorphic format|anamorphic lens]]es. These lenses produced a certain texture, one that lacked the sharpness of [[Panavision]]'s Primo anamorphic lenses.<ref name=asc />

Yeoman lit interior shots with tungsten incandescent fixtures and [[DMX512|DMX]]-dimmer-controlled lighting. The crew made the Warenhaus ceiling from stretched [[muslin]] rigged with twenty 4K [[hydrargyrum medium-arc iodide lamp|HMI]] lamps, an arrangement wherein the reflected light penetrated the [[skylight]], accentuating the set's daylighting. Yeoman preferred the lighting choice because the warm tungsten fixtures contrasted with the coolish daylight.<ref name=asc /> When shooting deliberately less inviting hotel sets, such as Zero and Gustave's small bedrooms and the Grand Budapest's [[servants' quarters]], the filmmakers combined [[fluorescent lighting]], [[paper lantern]]s, and bare [[incandescent lights]] for historical accuracy.<ref name=asc />

The [[Stuttgart]]-based LUXX Studios and [[Look Effects]]' German branch (also in Stuttgart) managed most of ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} visual effects, under the supervision of Gabriel Sanchez.<ref name=asc /><ref name=cgs /> Their work for the film comprised 300 shots, created by a small cadre of specialized artists.<ref name="cgs">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cgsociety.org/index.php/CGSFeatures/CGSFeatureSpecial/grand_budapest_hotel3 |title=The Grand Budapest Hotel |last=CGSociety staff |date=March 13, 2014 |website=CGSociety |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170509113357/http://www.cgsociety.org/index.php/CGSFeatures/CGSFeatureSpecial/grand_budapest_hotel3 |archive-date=May 9, 2017 |access-date=November 24, 2019}}</ref> The development of the film's effects was swift, but at times difficult. Sanchez did not work on set with Anderson as Look Effects opened their Stuttgart headquarters after ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' filming wrapped, and therefore was only able to reference his prior experience with the director. The California-based artist also became homesick working his first international assignment.<ref name=cgs /> Only four artists from the newly assembled team had experience working on a major studio set.<ref name=cgs /> 

Creation of the effects was daunting because of their technical demands. The filmmakers camouflaged some of the [[stop motion animation|stop-motion]] and matte effects in the forest-set chase scene to convey the desired intensity, and enhancing the snowscape with particle effects posed another challenge.<ref name=cgs /> Sanchez cites the observatory and hotel shots as work that best demonstrate his special effects team's ingenuity. To achieve the aging brutalist design of the 1968 Grand Budapest, they generated computer models supplemented with detailed lighting, matte effects and shadowy expanses.<ref name=cgs /> The crew used a similar technique in developing digital shots of the observatory; unlike the hotel, the observatory's base miniature was presented in pieces. They rendered the observatory with 20 different elements, data furthermore enhanced at Anderson's request. It took about one hour per shot to complete the final digital rendering.<ref name=cgs /> The filmmakers also used [[DaVinci Resolve]] to handle [[color grading]] tasks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://postperspective.com/enhancing-color-grand-budapest-hotel/|title=Enhancing color at 'The Grand Budapest Hotel'|first=Randi|last=Altman|work=postPerpective|date=March 20, 2014|access-date=August 9, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809050514/https://postperspective.com/enhancing-color-grand-budapest-hotel/|archive-date=August 9, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Set design===
[[File:The Grand Budapest Hotel maquette.jpg|thumb|left|alt=|Miniature model of the Grand Budapest Hotel exhibited at [[Cinémathèque française|Cinémathèque]], Paris (2025)]]

[[Adam Stockhausen]]—another Anderson associate—was responsible for ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} production design. He and Anderson collaborated previously on ''[[The Darjeeling Limited]]'' (2007) and ''Moonrise Kingdom''.<ref name="Seitz151">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=151}}</ref> Stockhausen researched the United States [[Library of Congress]]'s [[photochrom]] print collection of [[alps|alpine]] resorts to source ideas for the film's visual palette. These images showcased little of recognizable Europe, instead cataloging obscure historical landmarks unknown to the general public.<ref name="vice1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-grand-budapest-hotel-production-designer/ |title=We Talked to 'The Grand Budapest Hotel' Production Designer About Pastries, Postcards, and Taxidermy |last=Chung |first=Becky |date=February 9, 2015 |website=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |access-date=September 29, 2019 |archive-date=September 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190929201443/https://www.vice.com/en_us/article/78exvx/the-grand-budapest-hotel-production-designer |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Seitz163">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=163}}</ref> The resulting stylistic choice is a warm, bright visual palette pronounced by soft pastel tonalities. Some of ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' interior sets contrast this look in interior shots, primarily Schloss Lutz and the Checkpoint Nineteen prison: the imposing hardwoods, intense greens and golds of the Schloss Lutz evoke oppressive wealth, and the derelict Checkpoint Nineteen decays in a cool bluish-gray tint.<ref name=Seitz143 />

The filmmakers relied on [[matte (filmmaking)|matte paintings]] and [[miniature effect]] techniques to play on perspective for elaborate scenes, creating the illusion of size and grandeur. Under the leadership of Simon Weisse, scale models of structures were constructed by a Berlin-based propmaking team at Studio Babelsberg in tandem with the Görlitz shoot.<ref name="Cinefex">{{Cite news |url=https://cinefex.com/blog/the-grand-budapest-hotel/ |title=The Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Edwards |first=Graham |date=March 11, 2014 |newspaper=Cinefex Blog |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150218233732/http://cinefex.com/blog/the-grand-budapest-hotel/ |archive-date=February 18, 2015 |access-date=September 29, 2019}}</ref><ref name=NYT022814 /> Weisse joined ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} design staff after coming to the attention of production manager Miki Emmrich, with whom he worked on ''[[Cloud Atlas (film)|Cloud Atlas]]'' (2012).<ref name=Cinefex /> Anderson liked the novelty of miniatures, having used them in ''[[The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou]]'' (2004) and more extensively in ''[[Fantastic Mr. Fox (film)|Fantastic Mr. Fox]]'' (2009).<ref name="NYT022814">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/02/movies/the-miniature-model-behind-the-grand-budapest-hotel.html |title=You Can Look, but You Can't Check In |last=Murphy |first=Mekado |date=February 28, 2014 |website=The New York Times |access-date=March 14, 2014 |archive-date=June 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200624095008/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/02/movies/the-miniature-model-behind-the-grand-budapest-hotel.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Weisse and his propmakers built three major miniature models: the {{frac|1|8}}-scale forest set, the {{frac|1|12}}-scale observatory, and the [[1:18 scale|{{frac|1|18}}-scale]] Grand Budapest Hotel set, based on art director Carl Sprague's conceptual renderings. The Grand Budapest Hotel set comprised the hotel building atop a wooded ledge with a [[funicular]], bound by a [[Caspar David Friedrich|Friedrichian]] landscape painting superimposed with [[chroma key|green-screen]] technology.<ref name=NYT022814 /> Designers sculpted the {{convert|3|m|ft|adj=mid|-high|abbr=off|sp=us}} hotel with silicone resin molds and etched brass embellishment. Photos of the Warenhaus set were then glued in boxes installed to each window to convey the illusion of light.<ref name=Cinefex /> The funicular's 35-degree slope required a separate, lateral model.<ref name=Cinefex /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/artsandculture/article/18943/1/how-a-viennese-author-inspired-the-grand-budapest-hotel |title=How a Viennese author inspired The Grand Budapest Hotel |website=[[Dazed & Confused (magazine)|Dazed]] |date=February 27, 2014 |access-date=March 18, 2014 |archive-date=June 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200624093950/https://www.dazeddigital.com/artsandculture/article/18943/1/how-a-viennese-author-inspired-the-grand-budapest-hotel |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.stern.de/kultur/tv/wes-anderson-im-interview-die-deutsche-bahn-hat-die-besten-schlafwagen-2094502.html |title=Wes Anderson im Interview: ''Die Deutsche Bahn hat die besten Schlafwagen'' |date=March 6, 2014 |website=[[Stern (magazine)|Stern]] |access-date=April 10, 2014 |archive-date=April 18, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140418124240/http://www.stern.de/kultur/tv/wes-anderson-im-interview-die-deutsche-bahn-hat-die-besten-schlafwagen-2094502.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Timber, soldered brass, fine powdered sugar, and styrofoam were used to construct the observatory set, and [[Polyester Fiberfill|polyester fiberfill]] was the forest model's snow.<ref name=Cinefex />

The creation of ''[[Boy with Apple]]'' was a four-month-long process by English painter [[Michael Taylor (English artist)|Michael Taylor]], who was inspired by [[Renaissance painting|Renaissance]] [[portraiture]], among them ''[[Gabrielle d'Estrées et une de ses sœurs]]'' (1594).<ref name=week /><ref name="dodd">{{Cite web |url=https://www.waterhousedodd.com/news/39-michael-taylor-s-painting-boy-with-apple-to-play/ |title=Michael Taylor's painting Boy with Apple to play a central role in Wes Anderson's new film, The Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Staff |date=March 2, 2014 |website=Waterhouse and Dodd |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191130081143/https://www.waterhousedodd.com/news/39-michael-taylor-s-painting-boy-with-apple-to-play/ |archive-date=November 30, 2019 |access-date=November 28, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://lwlies.com/articles/the-grand-budapest-hotel-boy-with-apple-painting/|title=The story behind The Grand Budapest Hotel's 'Boy with Apple' painting|first=Adam|last=Woodward|work=[[Little White Lies (magazine)|Little White Lies]]|date=February 22, 2021|accessdate=October 9, 2024}}</ref> Taylor had been approached by one of the producers before receiving the script and reference material, and the film's artistic direction piqued his interest. The painter originally worked alone before deferring to Anderson for input when certain aspects of the painting deviated from the overall vision.<ref name=week /> Taylor stated that while he found the initial making difficult, he was able to forge an identity for ''Boy with Apple'' based on his lack of familiarity with Anderson's films.<ref name="week">{{Cite web |url=https://theweek.com/article/index/259203/the-untold-story-behind-the-grand-budapest-hotels-boy-with-apple |title=The untold story behind The Grand Budapest Hotel's "Boy with Apple" |last=Meslow |first=Scott |date=April 2, 2014 |website=[[The Week]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191128034235/https://theweek.com/articles/448412/untold-story-behind-grand-budapest-hotels-boy-apple |archive-date=November 28, 2019 |access-date=November 27, 2019}}</ref><ref name=dodd /> The producers' casting choice for ''Boy with Apple''{{'s}} subject was contingent on the character description of a blond-haired boy with the physique of a [[ballet]] dancer. They signed Ed Munro, an actor with a theater background, the day after his audition.<ref name=week /> The filmmakers staged the painting sessions at a [[Jacobean architecture|Jacobean]] boarding school, then empty for summer holiday, near Taylor's home in [[Dorset]]. Filmmakers dressed Munro in about 50 ornate costumes with velvet cloaks, [[codpiece]]s and furs, photographed each one, and submitted them to Anderson for approval. Munro, who maintained the same posture and facial expression for several hours, found the costuming uncomfortable.<ref name=week /> Another painting titled ''Two Lesbians Masturbating'', created by Rich Pellegrino, draws from the work of [[Expressionism|Expressionist]] artist [[Egon Schiele]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/530646/wes-anderson-art-show-inspires-wes-andersons-newest-film/|title=Wes Anderson Art Show Inspires Painting In Wes Anderson's New Film|first=Germain|last=Lussier|work=[[/Film]]|date=March 6, 2014|access-date=August 8, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250522103206/https://www.slashfilm.com/530646/wes-anderson-art-show-inspires-wes-andersons-newest-film/|archive-date=May 22, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/03/wes-anderson-on-grand-budapest-and-his-socks.html|title=Wes Anderson on The Grand Budapest Hotel, Reimagined Nazis, and His Sock Drawer|first=Jennifer|last=Vineyard|work=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]|date=March 12, 2014|access-date=August 8, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250808190207/https://www.vulture.com/2014/03/wes-anderson-on-grand-budapest-and-his-socks.html|archive-date=August 8, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Annie Atkins]] was ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} lead graphic designer.<ref name="Cr">{{Cite web |url=https://www.creativereview.co.uk/designing-for-the-grand-budapest-hotel/ |title=Designing for The Grand Budapest Hotel |date=March 11, 2014 |website=[[Creative Review]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312042705/https://www.creativereview.co.uk/cr-blog/2014/march/grand-budapest-hotel |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |access-date=February 26, 2020}}{{subscription required}}</ref> She devised Zubrowkan objects—newspapers, banknotes, police reports and passports—from reference material gathered from the location scouting. Atkins was a novice in film but had expertise in advertising design to reference, producing 20 sketches of a single artifact per day when the on-set shooting peaked.<ref name="Fc">{{Cite news |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/3027566/the-real-star-of-the-grand-budapest-hotel-graphic-design |title=The Real Star Of Wes Anderson's "The Grand Budapest Hotel"? Graphic Design |last=Rhodes |first=Margaret |date=March 14, 2014 |website=[[Fast Company]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227040005/https://www.fastcompany.com/3027566/the-real-star-of-the-grand-budapest-hotel-graphic-design |archive-date=February 27, 2020 |access-date=February 26, 2020}}</ref> She used an antique typewriter for the mock documents with a [[dip pen]] for the embellished handwriting.<ref name=Cr /> Among her early tasks was the creation of weathered, worn props for fidelity to the film's timeline. To achieve the appearance of prolonged exposure to air, Atkins blow dried paper dipped in tea.<ref name=Fc /> She said, "The beautiful thing about period filmmaking is that you're creating graphic design for a time before graphic designers existed, per se. It was really the craftsmen who were the designers: the blacksmith designed the lettering in the cast iron gates; the glazier sculpted the lettering in the stained glass; the sign-painter drew the lettering for the shopfronts; the printer chose the type blocks for the stationery."<ref name=Cr />

Pastries are an important motif in ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' story.<ref name=slate /> The signature ''courtesan au chocolat'' from Mendl's mirrors the French dessert ''[[religieuse]]'', a [[choux pastry|choux]]-based pastry with a mocha (or chocolate) glaze and vanilla custard filling.<ref name="slate">{{Cite web |url=http://www.slate.com/blogs/browbeat/2014/03/19/grand_budapest_hotel_pastries_recipe_what_it_s_like_to_make_wes_anderson.html |title=What It's Like to Bake Like Wes Anderson |last=Anderson |first=L. V. |date=March 19, 2014 |website=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227204701/https://slate.com/culture/2014/03/grand-budapest-hotel-pastries-recipe-what-its-like-to-make-wes-andersons-courtesans-au-chocolats.html |archive-date=February 27, 2020 |access-date=March 19, 2014}}</ref> A Görlitz pastry chef crafted the ''courtesan'' before working with Anderson on the final design.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/rachelysanders/make-the-pastry-from-the-grand-budapest-hotel |title=How To Make The Starring Pastry From Wes Anderson's New Movie |last=Sanders |first=Rachel |website=[[BuzzFeed]] |date=March 12, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227205027/https://www.buzzfeed.com/rachelysanders/make-the-pastry-from-the-grand-budapest-hotel |archive-date=February 27, 2020 |access-date=January 6, 2015}}</ref>

===Costumes===
[[File:FIDM Museum - Film costumes - Grand Budapest Hotel (16476925205).jpg|thumb|alt=Shot of a FIDM Museum costume exhibit, highlighted by Gustave's signature uniform and Madame D's ornate coat-and-gown ensemble| Madame D.'s centerpiece coat-and-gown ensemble at a [[Fashion Institute of Design & Merchandising Museum|FIDM Museum]] costume exhibit, Los Angeles (2015)]]

Veteran costume designer [[Milena Canonero]] endeavored to capture the essence of the film's characters.<ref name="vf2">{{Cite web |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2014/03/the-grand-budapest-hotel-fashion |title=Behind the Fashion in The Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Rado |first=Priya |date=March 7, 2014 |website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228083419/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2014/03/the-grand-budapest-hotel-fashion |archive-date=February 28, 2020 |access-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> Canonero researched 1930s uniform design and period artwork by photographers [[George Hurrell]] and [[Man Ray]] and painters [[Kees van Dongen]], [[Gustav Klimt]], [[George Grosz]] and [[Tamara de Lempicka]].<ref name=Seitz89 /> Canonero was also influenced by non-period literature and art.<ref name=vf2 /> Specialized artists then realized her designs in [[Photoshop]], allowing them to work closely to the actors' likenesses.<ref name=Seitz89 /> The filmmakers assembled most of the basic costumes in their Görlitz workshop, others from the Berlin-based Theaterkunst, and the uniforms came from a Polish workshop. They rented vintagewear for [[extra (acting)|extras]] in crowd shots.<ref name="Seitz89">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=89}}</ref> Canonero used dense [[mauve]] and deep-purple [[AW Hainsworth]] facecloth for the Grand Budapest uniforms instead of the more subdued colors typical of hospitality uniforms.<ref name=Seitz89 /> She researched diverse ideas for the gray-and-black military uniforms, in accordance with script specifications that they not be green or too historically identifiable.<ref name="lacostume">{{Cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-et-mn-en-costumes-budapest-20141204-story.html |title=The Envelope: Milena Canonero's 'Grand Budapest' costumes match Wes Anderson's vision |last=Kinosian |first=Janet |date=December 4, 2014 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228083027/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-et-mn-en-costumes-budapest-20141204-story.html |archive-date=February 28, 2020 |access-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> Anderson did most of the insignia, occasionally approving designs from Canonero's workshop in [[Rome]].<ref name=lacostume />

The filmmakers gave the characters distinct looks. They distinguished men with facial hair to enhance their style.<ref name=Seitz89 /> Gustave's wardrobe was intended to evoke "a sense of perfection and control" even in his collapsing livelihood.<ref name=Seitz90 /> Anderson and Canonero visualized Agatha with a Mexico-shaped facial birthmark, a wheat blade in her hair, and clothing to reflect her working class position and the brightness of her pastries.<ref name=lacostume /> Madame was dressed in a silk velvet coat-and-gown-ensemble with [[Gustav Klimt|Klimtesque]] handprint patterns and mink trim by [[Fendi]], from a previous professional relationship with Anderson and Canonero. Fendi developed the gray astrakhan fur overcoat for Norton's Albert, and loaned other furs to assist the needs of the shoot.<ref name=lacostume /><ref name="Seitz90">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|p=90}}</ref> To age Swinton, makeup artist Mark Coulier applied soft silicone rubber prosthetics encapsulated in dissolvable plastic molding on her face.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2015/02/grand-budapest-hotel-makeup-oscar |title=How to Turn Tilda Swinton Into an Old Lady, With Enough Liver Spots to Make Wes Anderson Happy |last=Rich |first=Katey |date=February 13, 2015 |website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228161055/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2015/02/grand-budapest-hotel-makeup-oscar |archive-date=February 28, 2020 |access-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> Dafoe's Jopling wore a [[Prada]] leather coat inspired by outerwear for military [[dispatch rider]]s, adorned with custom silver knuckle pieces from jeweler Waris Ahluwalia (a close friend of Anderson's).<ref name=Seitz90 /> Canonero modified the coat with fine red-wool stitching and a weapons compartment inside the front lapel.<ref name=Seitz90 />

===Music===
{{Main|The Grand Budapest Hotel (soundtrack){{!}}''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' (soundtrack)}}

Anderson recruited [[Alexandre Desplat]] to compose the film's [[Russian folk music|Russian folk]]-influenced score encompassing symphonic compositions and background [[drone (music)|drones]];<ref name="Reed2014">{{Cite magazine |last=Reed |first=Ryan |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/stream-wes-andersons-grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-20140226 |title=Stream Wes Anderson's ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' Soundtrack |date=February 26, 2014 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |access-date=March 30, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140314153208/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/stream-wes-andersons-grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-20140226 |archive-date=March 14, 2014}}</ref> the [[balalaika]] formed the score's musical core.<ref name="balalaika">{{Cite news |last=Danton |first=Eric R. |url=https://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2014/02/18/grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-relies-on-original-music-song-premiere/ |title=''Grand Budapest Hotel'' Soundtrack Relies On Original Music (Song Premiere) |date=February 18, 2014 |work=The Wall Street Journal |url-access=subscription |access-date=February 23, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223223932/http://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2014/02/18/grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-relies-on-original-music-song-premiere/ |archive-date=February 23, 2015}}</ref> Anderson and music supervisor [[Randall Poster]] spent about six months consulting experts to hone their vision.<ref name=indscore /> Its score's classical roots make ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' unique among Anderson-directed projects, forgoing the writer-director's usual practice of employing contemporary [[pop music]].<ref name="indscore">{{Cite news |last=Jagernauth |first=Kevin |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2014/06/exclusive-pics-of-recording-sessions-for-grand-budapest-hotel-randall-poster-talks-score-wes-anderson-more-84671/ |title=Exclusive: Pics Of Recording Sessions For 'Grand Budapest Hotel,' Randall Poster Talks Score, Wes Anderson & More |date=June 19, 2014 |work=Indiewire |access-date=February 28, 2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229004445/https://www.indiewire.com/2014/06/exclusive-pics-of-recording-sessions-for-grand-budapest-hotel-randall-poster-talks-score-wes-anderson-more-84671/ |archive-date=February 29, 2020}}</ref> Desplat felt his exposure to Anderson's filmmaking style was integral to articulating an Eastern European musical approach for the film's score.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lacombe |first=Bridgette |url=https://www.filmmusicmag.com/?p=13888 |title=Interview with Alexandre Desplat |date=December 4, 2014 |work=Film Music |access-date=February 28, 2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228233449/http://www.filmmusicmag.com/?p=13888 |archive-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> His direction expanded on some of the sounds and instrumentation of ''Fantastic Mr. Fox'' and ''Moonrise Kingdom''. As well, the scope of Desplat's responsibilities entailed differentiating ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} sprawling cast of characters with distinctive melodic themes and motifs.<ref name="Seitz135">{{harvnb|Seitz|2015|pp=135–136}}</ref> [[ABKCO Records]] released the 32-track score digitally on March 4, 2014.<ref name="Davis2014">{{Cite news |last=Davis |first=Edward |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/alexandre-desplat-more-wes-andersons-the-grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-arrives-on-march-4-20140123 |title=Alexandre Desplat & More: Wes Anderson's 'The Grand Budapest Hotel' Soundtrack Arrives On March 4th |date=January 23, 2014 |work=Indiewire |access-date=March 30, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160427042959/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/alexandre-desplat-more-wes-andersons-the-grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-arrives-on-march-4-20140123 |archive-date=April 27, 2016}}</ref> It featured sampled recordings<ref name="npr">{{Cite web |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/deceptivecadence/2015/02/19/387535508/composing-the-folk-music-of-a-made-up-country |title=Composing The Folk Music Of A Made-Up Country |last=Blair |first=Elizabeth |date=February 19, 2015 |website=[[NPR]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229165021/https://www.npr.org/sections/deceptivecadence/2015/02/19/387535508/composing-the-folk-music-of-a-made-up-country |archive-date=February 29, 2020 |access-date=February 29, 2020}}</ref> and contributions from orchestras such as the [[Osipov State Russian Folk Orchestra]] and a 50-person ensemble of French and Russian balalaika players.<ref name=indscore /><ref name="pitchfork2014">{{Cite news |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/54108-stream-wes-andersons-the-grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-on-pitchfork-advance/ |title=Stream Wes Anderson's The Grand Budapest Hotel Soundtrack on Pitchfork Advance |date=February 25, 2014 |access-date=March 30, 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202190038/https://pitchfork.com/news/54108-stream-wes-andersons-the-grand-budapest-hotel-soundtrack-on-pitchfork-advance/ |archive-date=February 2, 2018 |website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]}}</ref>

==Themes and style==

The reticent Anderson did not discuss themes in interviews conducted during the press junkets, lending several interpretations of ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://filmschoolrejects.com/how-wes-anderson-built-the-grand-budapest-hotel-bd6690ab9199/ |title=How Wes Anderson Built 'The Grand Budapest Hotel' |last=Giroux |first=Jack |date=March 6, 2014 |website=[[Film School Rejects]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200305213939/https://filmschoolrejects.com/how-wes-anderson-built-the-grand-budapest-hotel-bd6690ab9199/ |archive-date=March 5, 2020 |access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref> The film has been read as work that examines tragedy, war, fascism, and nostalgia.<ref name=queen /><ref name=atlantic3 /><ref name="Ny3">{{Cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/07/movies/wes-andersons-grand-budapest-hotel-is-a-complex-caper.html |title=Bittersweet Chocolate on the Pillow |last=Scott |first=A.O. |date=March 6, 2014 |website=The New York Times |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200305213003/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/07/movies/wes-andersons-grand-budapest-hotel-is-a-complex-caper.html |archive-date=March 5, 2020 |access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref>

===Nostalgia and fascism===

Nostalgia is a major theme in Anderson's repertoire.<ref name="Dilley29">{{harvnb|Dilley|2017|p=29}}</ref> ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' universe is envisioned with nostalgic yearning, where characters perpetuate the "illusion of a time where they don't belong",<ref name="queen"/> the consequence of not so much the recapture of a vanished era than a romanticizing of the past.<ref name="salon">{{Cite web |url=https://www.salon.com/2014/04/02/up_in_the_old_hotel_the_hidden_meaning_of_wes_andersons_nostalgia/ |title=Up in the old hotel: The hidden meaning of Wes Anderson's nostalgia |last=Levitz |first=Eric |date=April 3, 2014 |website=[[Salon (website)|Salon]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200305211746/https://www.salon.com/2014/04/02/up_in_the_old_hotel_the_hidden_meaning_of_wes_andersons_nostalgia/ |archive-date=March 5, 2020 |access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref><ref name="nyer2">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2014/03/10/lost-time |title=Lost Time |last=Denby |first=David |date=March 3, 2014 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20170206130657/http://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2014/03/10/lost-time |archive-date=February 6, 2017 |access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref><ref name=av /> One theory among critics suggests "profound" subtext of the science of human memory within the film's [[story within a story|nonlinear]] narrative structure,<ref name="Dilley463">{{harvnb|Dilley|2017|p=463}}</ref> whereas others saw ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' as an introspection of Anderson's sensibilities both as a writer and as a director.<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://lwlies.com/reviews/the-grand-budapest-hotel/ |title= The Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Jenkins |first=David |date=March 6, 2014 |website=[[Little White Lies (magazine)|Little White Lies]] |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200614121842/https://lwlies.com/reviews/the-grand-budapest-hotel/ |archive-date=June 14, 2020 |access-date=June 14, 2020}}</ref>

''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' does not directly refer to historical events; rather, oblique references contextualize the real-time history.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2014/03/grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson-whimsical-fascists-nazis/ |title=The Whimsical Fascists of Wes Anderson's "The Grand Budapest Hotel" |last=Suebsaeng |first=Asawin |date=March 14, 2014 |website=[[Mother Jones (magazine)|Mother Jones]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200305170032/https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2014/03/grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson-whimsical-fascists-nazis/ |archive-date=March 5, 2020 |access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref> The most deliberate of these references allude to [[Nazism]]. In perhaps the film's most dramatic display of corrupt power, the Zubrowkan military invasion of the Grand Budapest, and the fascist emblems of the hotel lobby's newly adorned tapestry, mirror scenes from [[Leni Riefenstahl]]'s propaganda film ''[[Triumph of the Will]]'' (1935).<ref name=Allude/> Gustave's black-and-white stripes evoke the uniforms of the concentration camp prisoners, and his steadfast commitment to his job becomes an act of defiance that threatens to jeopardize his life.<ref name=Allude>{{Cite news |last=Adams |first=Sam |url= https://www.indiewire.com/2014/03/the-grand-budapest-hotel-isnt-just-wes-andersons-best-movie-its-a-breakthrough-126776/ |title= "The Grand Budapest Hotel" Isn't (Just) Wes Anderson's Best Movie: It's a Breakthrough |date=March 7, 2014 |work=Indiewire |access-date=April 25, 2020 |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200425064116/https://www.indiewire.com/2014/03/the-grand-budapest-hotel-isnt-just-wes-andersons-best-movie-its-a-breakthrough-126776/ |archive-date=April 25, 2020}}</ref> ''[[The Atlantic]]''{{'s}} [[Norm Eisen|Norman L. Eisen]], who is among the people listed in "Special Thanks" at the end of the film, called ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' a cautionary tale of the consequences of [[the Holocaust]], a story that examines Nazi motivations while traversing [[Post-war|postwar]] European history through comedy. He contends that certain main characters symbolize both the oppressed — the openly [[Bisexuality|bisexual]] Gustave, the [[Person of color|nonwhite]] refugee Zero, and the [[Jews|Jewish]] Kovacs — and the oppressor in Dmitri, overseer of a fascist, [[Schutzstaffel|SS]]-like organization.<ref name="atlantic3">{{Cite web |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2015/02/how-grand-budapest-hotel-pays-tribute-to-the-holocaust/385264/ |title=The Grand Budapest Hotel Is a Thoughtful Comedy About Tragedy |last=Eisen |first=Norman |date=February 20, 2015 |website=[[The Atlantic]] |url-access=limited |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200305164857/https://www.theatlantic.com/entertainment/archive/2015/02/how-grand-budapest-hotel-pays-tribute-to-the-holocaust/385264/ |archive-date=March 5, 2020 |access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref> Film critic Daniel Garrett argues Gustave defies fascist notions of human perfection because he embraces the flaws of his peers, despite his own expertise: "Gustave is not surprised by feelings of anxiety or desire, or contemptuous of a scarred or crippled body; and he shares his values with his staff, with Zero. Gustave sees the heart and the effort, the spirit, despite his regard for excellence, ritual, and style."<ref name=offscreen /> According to the academic Donna Kornhaber, ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' reinforces the increasingly scathing critique of [[Collectivism and individualism|collectivism]] defining late period Anderson films.<ref name="Kornhaber2323">{{harvnb|Kornhaber|2017|pp=250–251}}</ref>

===Friendship and loyalty===
Another principal topic of discussion among critics has been ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} exploration of friendship and loyalty. Zero appears to be Gustave's only true friend, and his unwavering devotion (at first, a mentor-protégé relationship) establishes the film's strongest bond.<ref name=queen /><ref name="offscreen">{{Cite magazine |last=Garrett |first=Daniel |date=November 2016 |title=Charm, Courage, and Eruptions of Vulgar Force: Wes Anderson's The Grand Budapest Hotel |magazine=Offscreen |language=en |location=Canada |volume=20 |issn=1712-9559 }}</ref> Gustave is underwhelmed by Zero but is increasingly empathetic to his newly-hired mentee's plight in their subsequent exploits, united by their shared enthusiasm for the hotel—so much that he defends Zero against police thuggery and rewards his loyalty with his inheritance.<ref name="queen">{{Cite magazine |last=Marshall |first=Lee |date=Summer 2014 |title=The Budapest Hotel: Wes Anderson's Fabulous Fancy |magazine=[[Queen's Quarterly]] |language=en |location=Kingston, Ontario |volume=121 |pages=242–251 }}</ref><ref name="nyer">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/the-grand-budapest-hotel-wes-andersons-artistic-manifesto |title="The Grand Budapest Hotel": Wes Anderson's Artistic Manifesto |last=Brody |first=Richard |date=March 7, 2014 |magazine=The New Yorker |access-date=March 1, 2020 |archive-date=April 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200411132409/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/the-grand-budapest-hotel-wes-andersons-artistic-manifesto |url-status=live }}</ref> Zero's less-central romance with Agatha is as constant a presence as his friendship with Gustave; he continues operating the hotel in his dead lover's memory, despite the slain Gustave representing the Grand Budapest's spirit.<ref name=queen /> The subject matter's emphasis of love, friendship, and the intertwining tales of nobility, dignity, and self-control, ''[[The New Yorker]]''{{'s}} [[Richard Brody]] argues, forms the "very soul of a moral politics that transcends accidents of circumstance and particular historical incidents".<ref name=nyer />

Kornhaber contends the focus on the dynamic of a mismatched pairing forms the crux of ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} central theme.<ref name="Kornhaber2356"/> The unusual circumstance of the Gustave–Zero friendship seems to reflect an attachment to "an idea of historical and cultural belonging that they find ultimately to be best expressed through one another", and by proxy, the two men discover a fundamental kinship through their shared esteem of the Grand Budapest.<ref name="Kornhaber2356">{{harvnb|Kornhaber|2017|pp=253–254}}</ref>

===Color===

''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} use of color accentuates narrative tones and conveys visual emphasis to the subject matter and passage of time. The film eschews Anderson's trademark pale yellow for a sharp palette of vibrant reds, pinks and purples in pre-war Grand Budapest scenes. The composition fades as the timeline forebodes impending war, sometimes in complete black-and-white in scenes exploring Zero's memory of wartime, underscoring the gradual tonal shift. Subdued beiges, orange, and pale blue characterize the visual palette of post-war Grand Budapest scenes, manifesting the hotel's diminished prestige.<ref name=queen />

''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' was released in France on February 26, 2014, preceding the film's global rollout. General release expanded to Germany, Belgium, the United Kingdom, the United States (March 7), and two other international markets the second week.<ref name="France">{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/03/international-box-office-frozen-crossing-1-billion-worldwide-692038/ |title=Update: International Box Office: 'The Hobbit: The Desolation Of Smaug' Has No. 1 Japan Opening; 'Lego' Builds to $121M Overseas; 'Frozen' Crossing $1B Worldwide; 'Robocop' Takes $20.5M In China; More |last=Tartaglione |first=Nancy |date=March 3, 2014 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200306025354/https://deadline.com/2014/03/international-box-office-frozen-crossing-1-billion-worldwide-692038/ |archive-date=March 6, 2020 |access-date=March 5, 2020}}</ref> ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' opened to a few US theaters as part of a month-long limited platform release, initially screening from four arthouse theaters in New York and Los Angeles.<ref name=Specialty /> After the [[87th Academy Awards]]' nominations announcement, Fox re-expanded the film's theater presence for a brief, multi-city re-release campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2015/01/grand-budapest-hotel-rerelease-oscars-1201351608/ |title='Grand Budapest Hotel' Checks Back Into Theaters After Oscar Nom Haul |last=Hipes |first=Patrick |date=January 16, 2015 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200316162048/https://deadline.com/2015/01/grand-budapest-hotel-rerelease-oscars-1201351608/ |archive-date=March 16, 2020 |access-date=March 16, 2020}}</ref>

|url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/dvd/the-grand-budapest-hotel/ |title=Blu-ray Review: The Grand Budapest Hotel |last=Bowen |first=Chuck |date=June 18, 2014 |website=[[Slant Magazine]] |url=https://www.the-numbers.com/home-market/packaged-media-sales-chart/2014/06/22 |title=United States Combined DVD and Blu-ray Sales Chart for Week Ending June 22, 2014 |date=June 22, 2014 [[The Criterion Collection]] released a director-approved special edition Blu-ray and DVD of the film on April 28, 2020. The discs include audio commentary from Anderson, Goldblum, producer [[Roman Coppola]], and film critic Kent Jones; storyboard animatics, a behind-the-scenes documentary, video essays, and previously unaired cast and crew interviews.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.criterion.com/films/29601-the-grand-budapest-hotel |title=The Grand Budapest Hotel |website=[[The Criterion Collection]] |access-date=January 17, 2020 |archive-date=September 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200912160544/https://www.criterion.com/films/29601-the-grand-budapest-hotel |url-status=live }}</ref> It was released on [[Ultra HD Blu-ray]] by Criterion on September 30, 2025, as part of the ten film collection ''The Wes Anderson Archive: Ten Films, Twenty-Five Years''.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Zavaleta |first=Jonathan |date=2025-06-02 |title=The $500 Wes Anderson Criterion Box Set Is Cinephile Catnip |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/product-recommendations/lifestyle/wes-anderson-criterion-box-set-where-to-buy-1235352817/ |access-date=2025-06-03 |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===

''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' was considered a surprise box office success.<ref name="labox">{{Cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/cotown/la-et-mn-wes-anderson-grand-budapest-hotel-box-office-20140323-story.html |title=Wes Anderson's 'Grand Budapest Hotel' builds at the box |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200313085641/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/cotown/la-et-mn-wes-anderson-grand-budapest-hotel-box-office-20140323-story.html |archive-date=March 13, 2020 |access-date=March 13, 2020}}</ref> The film's performance plateaued in North America after a strong start, but finished the theatrical run as Anderson's highest-grossing film in the region.<ref name=guardgross /><ref name="Deadbox3">{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2015/01/the-grand-budapest-hotel-ps-1201345744/ |title='The Grand Budapest Hotel' Tops Specialty B.O.'s Top 10 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200313091133/https://deadline.com/2015/01/the-grand-budapest-hotel-ps-1201345744/ |archive-date=March 13, 2020 |access-date=March 13, 2020}}</ref> It performed strongest in key European and Asian markets.<ref name="guardgross">{{Cite news |last=Beaumont-Thomas |first=Ben |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/apr/16/the-grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson-highest-grossing |title=The Grand Budapest Hotel becomes Wes Anderson's highest-grossing film |date=April 16, 2014 |work=The Guardian |access-date=March 12, 2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200313041154/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2014/apr/16/the-grand-budapest-hotel-wes-anderson-highest-grossing |archive-date=March 13, 2020 }}</ref><ref name=wrapgross /> Germany was the most lucrative market, and the film's link to that country boosted the box office performance.<ref name=wrapgross /> South Korea, Australia, Spain, France, and the United Kingdom represented some of the film's largest takings.<ref name="wrapgross">{{Cite news |last=Cunningham |first=Todd |url=https://www.thewrap.com/grand-budapest-hotel-clicks-box-office-germany-shot/ |title='Grand Budapest Hotel' Clicks at Box Office in Germany, Where It Was Filmed |date=April 4, 2014 |archive-date=March 14, 2020}}</ref> ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' earned $59.3&nbsp;million (34.3 percent of its earnings) in the United States and Canada and $113.7&nbsp;million (65.7 percent) overseas, for a worldwide total of $173&nbsp;million,<ref name="BOM" /> making it the 46th-highest-grossing film of 2014,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2014/ |title=2014 Worldwide Box Office |website=Box Office Mojo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221219044236/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2014/ |archive-date=December 19, 2022 |access-date=March 12, 2020}}</ref> and Anderson's highest-grossing film to date.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Khatchatourian |first=Maane |url=https://variety.com/2014/film/box-office/grand-budapest-hotel-hits-100-mil-becomes-wes-andersons-highest-grossing-pic-1201157267/ |title='Grand Budapest Hotel' Hits $100 Mil, Becomes Wes The film posted $2.8&nbsp;million from 172 theaters during its opening week in France, trailing ''[[Supercondriaque]]'' and ''[[Non-Stop (film)|Non-Stop]]''. In Paris, ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' screenings were the weekend's biggest numbers.<ref name=France /> The film's $16,220 per-theater average was the best opening for any Anderson-directed project in France to date.<ref name=Specialty /> In its second week the number of theaters grew to 192, and ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' grossed another $1.64&nbsp;million at the French box office.<ref name=Deadbox4 /> Earnings dropped by just 30 percent the following weekend, for a total gross of $1.1&nbsp;million.<ref name="Deadbox5">{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/03/international-box-office-need-for-speed-revs-up-45-6m-rise-of-an-empire-adds-41-3m-for-158m-overseas-cume-frozen-has-big-japan-opening-will-it-beat-toy-story-3-for-all-time-animation-record-699919/ |title=Update: Intl Box Office: 'Rise Of An Empire' Cumes $159.6M; Universal's Spanish Comedy Breaks Records; 'Need For Speed' China Haul Outpaces Domestic; 'Frozen' Hot In Japan; More |last=Tartaglione |first=Nancy |date=March 17, 2014 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200314051942/https://deadline.com/2014/03/international-box-office-need-for-speed-revs-up-45-6m-rise-of-an-empire-adds-41-3m-for-158m-overseas-cume-frozen-has-big-japan-opening-will-it-beat-toy-story-3-for-all-time-animation-record-699919/ |archive-date=March 14, 2020 |access-date=March 13, 2020}}</ref> By March 24, the box office posted a five percent increase, and ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} French release had taken $8.2&nbsp;million overall.<ref name=Deadbox6 />

The week of March 6 saw ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' take $6.2&nbsp;million from 727 theaters internationally, yielding the most robust figures in Belgium ($156,000, from 12 theaters), Austria ($162,000, from 29 theaters), Germany ($1.138&nbsp;million, from 163 theaters), and the United Kingdom (top-three debut, with £1.53&nbsp;million or $1.85&nbsp;million from 284 theaters).<ref name="Deadbox4">{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/03/international-box-office-300-rise-of-an-empire-seeks-world-domination-opens-no-1-in-france-12-years-looking-at-oscar-bump-695156/ |title=Update: Intl Box Office: '300: Rise Of An Empire' Lifts To $88.8M; 'Non-Stop' Passes $100M Worldwide; More |last=Tartaglione |first=Nancy |date=March 10, 2014 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] In the United States, ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' opened to a $202,792-per theater average from a four-theater $811,166 overall gross, breaking the record for most robust live-action limited release previously held by [[Paul Thomas Anderson]]'s ''[[The Master (2012 film)|The Master]]'' (2012).<ref name="ptagross">{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/03/grand-budapest-hotel-box-office-debut-record-696110/ |title=Box Office: 'Grand Budapest Hotel' Checks In With Record Per-Screen Average |last=Brooks |first=Brian |date=March 9, 2014 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20200314154750/https://deadline.com/2014/03/grand-budapest-hotel-box-office-debut-record-696110/ |archive-date=March 14, 2020 |access-date=March 14, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/03/box-office-300-rise-of-an-empire-commands-40m-mr-peabody-chases-in-30m-son-of-god-may-fall-55-or-more-in-second-weekend-695863/ |title=Box Office Final: '300: Rise Of An Empire' Commands $45M; 'Mr. Peabody' Chases In $32.2M; 'Son Of God' Falls 59% In Second Weekend, 'Budapest Hotel' Per Screen Stuns With Over $202K |last=Busch |first=Anita |date=March 10, 2014 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=March 14, 2020 |archive-date=October 10, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181010130203/https://deadline.com/2014/03/box-office-300-rise-of-an-empire-commands-40m-mr-peabody-chases-in-30m-son-of-god-may-fall-55-or-more-in-second-weekend-695863/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The return, exceeding Fox's expectations for the weekend, was the best US opening for an Anderson-directed project to date.<ref name=ptagross /> ''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' also eclipsed ''Moonrise Kingdom''{{'s}} $130,749 per-theater average, hitherto Anderson's highest-opening limited release.<ref name=ptagross /> Fading interest in films hoping to capitalize on [[Academy Awards]] prestige and its crossover appeal to younger, casual moviegoers were crucial to ''The Grand Budapest Hotel''{{'s}} early box office success.<ref name=ptagross /> The film sustained the box office momentum as large suburban cineplexes were added to its limited run, racking $3.6&nbsp;million the second week and $6.7&nbsp;million the following weekend.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2014/03/box-office-wes-anderson-grand-budapest-hotel-bad-words-le-week-end-699948/ |title=Specialty Box Office: 'Grand Budapest Hotel' Checks In With Lofty $55K PTA In Expansion; ===Critical response===
{{Quote box |bgcolor=#FFFFF0 |salign=center |width=195px |align=right | quote = Mr. Anderson is no realist. Scott]], ''[[The New York Times]]'''''<ref name=Ny3 />}}

''The Grand Budapest Hotel'' received widespread critical acclaim and various critics selected the film in their end-of-2014 lists.<ref name="Best2014">{{Cite web reviewers; Gustave, for example, was described as a man "of convincing feelings", "sweetly wistful",<ref name=larev /><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/entertainment/movies/lsquothe-grand-budapest-hotelrsquo-itrsquos-a-trip/ |title=''The Grand Budapest Hotel'': It's a trip |last=Macdonald |first=Moira |date=March 13,
